question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{x}+3.$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{x}+3
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y}+3.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y}+3 \\ \frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y} & =x-3 \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =2(x-3) \\ (\sqrt[3]{y})^{3} & ={(2(x-3))}^{3} \\ y & =8(x-3)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=8(x-3)^{3}.
$$
